content.value_statement: Generic interface output can ignore an existing visual system and repeat familiar page patterns. Hallmark guides design, audits, redesigns, and reference studies with structured choices, reusable tokens, and responsive checks.
actual_capabilities: Creates a page design plan with genre, theme, macrostructure, navigation, footer, and enrichment choices.
Audits a named interface against documented visual and interaction anti-patterns without editing it.
Redesigns an existing interface while preserving routes, content intent, and implementation boundaries.
Studies a user-provided screenshot or public URL to describe reusable design DNA without copying pixels.
Checks existing project tokens, fonts, framework, spacing, and motion conventions before design work.
Requires interactive components to cover default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, and success states.
limitations: It provides design guidance and generated artifacts; it does not independently validate rendered pages in every browser.
URL study mode cannot assess visual rhythm from HTML alone and may require a screenshot.
It does not copy proprietary page pixels, source code, or template marketplace designs.
It needs user confirmation for destructive changes or a full rebuild of an existing implementation.

use_cases.title: Build a new product page
use_cases.description: Choose a distinct page structure, token system, and interaction approach for a new product or service.

use_cases.title: Audit an existing interface
use_cases.description: Produce a ranked list of visual, responsive, and interaction issues without changing the target.

use_cases.title: Extract design direction from a reference
use_cases.description: Study a user-provided screenshot or public page and adapt its design principles to original content.

prompt_templates.title: Design a landing page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Hallmark to design a landing page for a meal planning app. The audience is busy parents. Use a warm, practical tone.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Hallmark audit on the checkout button component. List visual, accessibility, and state issues. Do not edit files.

prompt_templates.title: Redesign within boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Hallmark redesign for the pricing page. Preserve the route, existing copy intent, and React component ownership. Propose the files you will change first.

prompt_templates.title: Study a reference safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Hallmark study on this screenshot. Extract macrostructure, type roles, colour anchor, and interaction ideas. Apply the principles to my original brand.

output_examples.input: Design a landing page for a developer tool.
output: A selected genre, theme, and macrostructure
A responsive page plan with named design tokens
A self-critique against visual quality gates
A ranked issue list with severity and rationale
Reusable structure, typography, and colour principles
Known evidence gaps for URL-only analysis
Original implementation direction rather than copied pixels

best_practices: Provide the audience, primary task, tone, and existing brand constraints before requesting a design.
Ask for a file-level plan before redesigning an established project.
Use screenshots when rhythm, density, or visual pacing matters in a reference study.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to copy a competitor page or a template marketplace design.
Do not request a full rebuild when a targeted visual change is sufficient.
Do not treat generated metrics, testimonials, or customer logos as factual content.

faq.question: What does Hallmark do?
faq.answer: Hallmark guides original web interface design, audits, redesigns, and visual reference studies.

faq.question: Can it change an existing application?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to preserve implementation boundaries unless you approve broader changes.

faq.question: Does audit mode edit files?
faq.answer: No. Audit mode returns a ranked improvement list and does not edit the target.

faq.question: Can it study a website URL?
faq.answer: Yes, for public pages that pass its URL safety checks. A screenshot is needed when the page is unreadable.

faq.question: Does it copy reference designs?
faq.answer: No. It extracts design principles and directs an original implementation using your content.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The package declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
